velocity_note: RECONCILED BEFORE QUOTING, per the PLAT-10 gate, and the three figures DISAGREE in a way that is information rather than a defect. AS-SCOPED from docs/sprints/sprint-05.json: 19 items, 81 points. COMPUTED by the tracker: planned 108, completed 45, parked 23, moved out 30, unfinished 40, across 18 items still in the sprint. The 27-point gap is named rather than smoothed: nine items were drawn in AFTER the sprint started - PLAT-16, DES-14, DES-15, DES-16, UI-12, UI-14, UI-15, UI-16, COPY-01 - because /startsprint's Step 0 backlog read found items the CEO had never shown the owner at planning. The owner had approved 81 points believing that was the full carried-forward scope. MOVED OUT is 30 points across 10 items, reported although the departures are all deliberate: the nine above plus SEO-14, pushed to the backlog at close because they were never dispatched. Velocity is therefore 45 of 108, 42%. A HONEST READING OF THAT NUMBER: the sprint dispatched 14 of 28 items and never dispatched the other 14, so this is not a sprint that under-delivered on what it attempted - it is a sprint that attempted half of what it scoped, because the session ended before wave 2. Of the 14 dispatched, 10 completed, 2 are blocked on the owner, 1 parked at its gate and 1 parked one article short.
sizing_accuracy: No DoD was narrowed, and two items were HELD SHORT of done rather than rounded up - which is the behaviour the standard exists to produce. SEO-13 took FAQ coverage from 47-present/39-absent to 74+-present/1-absent with 14 articles reasoned not-applicable by slug, and was PARKED anyway because its own census exits 1 on one absent article; the gap is an article CONT-13 published mid-sprint, so the corpus outran the item. UI-17 built the rail and proved it with computed getBoundingClientRect, then reported 'NOT MET, NOT NARROWED: the SUMBER clause is unachievable on 52 of 86 articles and needs a CEO decision' - it refused to decide its own DoD down, which is exactly right. TWO ITEMS WERE MIS-SIZED, both under. UI-18 at 5pt was scoped from a FALSE PREMISE the CEO wrote ('DALAM ARTIKEL INI appears on 0 of 85') and turned into a premise correction, a floor change, a relabel, a committed CI gate and two self-caught near-misses. PLAT-18 at 3pt was reversed by the review gate, went back, and returned with a repository-level create-mode refusal, a cross-scope collision check, an evidence-preservation gate on every mutating path, and a NUL byte removed from sprint-cli.ts that had made grep skip the file as binary for two days.

learnings.finding: FIVE ITEMS LANDED CORRECT WORK ON A BRANCH NOBODY READS, and it is one repository-shaped trap rather than five mistakes. CONT-13 (29 commits), CONT-14, RIGHTS-02 and RIGHTS-03 pushed their paper trails to their own feature branches; DES-17 opened PR #37 from the docs line INTO master. The site and docs spaces are ONE git repository kept apart by convention, so 'push your branch' and 'open a PR' both land somewhere plausible and wrong. PR #37 carried 100 files, 51 of them docs-space, and merging it would have moved the company record into the site source - the exact hazard RISK-09's guard exists to refuse, proposed by the agent as the way to finish its item. Every one was merged onto the docs line by the CEO, three-way, each after a test merge proving the earlier items' work survives.
learnings.file_changed: skillcentral/skills/hellokahwin/scripts/dispatch-agent.ps1 brief template and the /startsprint brief section - the dispatch must state the target integration branch per space, not leave it to the agent
learnings.why: The boundary guard refuses a cross-space CHECKOUT. It does not refuse a cross-space PR or a push to a feature branch, and those are how the work actually went astray. A guard that covers one verb reads as covering the hazard.

learnings.finding: THE CEO'S AD-HOC MEASUREMENTS LOST TO COMMITTED INSTRUMENTS SIX TIMES IN ONE SESSION, and every single time the instrument was right. A grep for REKOD in src/ returned nothing on a repo serving it 24 times (the source is RekodPanel). A credit regex captured RSC payload junk and missed 'berita harian', reporting an agent wrong when it was right. A census script run without --fetch crashed with exit 1 and was read as 'the gate fired'. An h2 count put 6 articles in violation where UI-18's committed gate reports none. Two worktree classifiers labelled six LIVE Sprint 05 trees as delete candidates. A final verification printed '!! MISSING' for all 18 registered worktrees from a broken sed.
learnings.file_changed: hellokahwin scripts/measure/classify-orphan-worktrees.py and scripts/measure/orphan-blob-check.py (both committed this sprint), plus the verification section of ceo-hellokahwin.md
learnings.why: The pattern is not carelessness, it is that a shell one-liner typed fresh each time has no regression suite and no negative control, while every gate this company shipped does. The rule that follows is narrower and cheaper than 'be careful': when an agent's committed gate disagrees with a CEO shell check, the gate wins until the CEO can show the gate failing on a case it should catch.

learnings.finding: THE BRIEF TEMPLATE POISONED EVERY WATCHER IN THE FLEET. The wave-1 brief printed the completion sentinel 'ITEM EXIT: 0' verbatim in a code fence, and the watcher matches that line anchored - so an agent tripped its own watcher merely by DISPLAYING its brief. Seven false wakes across four agents in the first forty minutes, every one still WORKING. Three further classes then appeared that no brief edit can fix: 'COMMIT EXIT: 0' from a commit script, 'HTTP/1.1 301' from an item's own curl, and 'UILINT EXIT: 1' from UI-06's gate reporting violations correctly mid-run - which Sprint 04's retro predicted BY NAME.
learnings.file_changed: the wave-1 briefs were de-poisoned in commit 04c2f7c; the durable fix is PLAT-13, carried to Sprint 06 with all four classes recorded as its must-not-fire set
learnings.why: Every gate this company ships adds a new well-formed 'NAME EXIT: n' string, so the must-not-fire set grows every sprint while the must-fire set stays at exactly one. That is an argument the matcher cannot win: the ITEM's completion needs a token no gate can collide with, such as a per-dispatch nonce.

learnings.finding: PERSONA EDITS MADE INSIDE A WORKTREE REACH NOTHING, and every dispatched agent works in a worktree. .claude/agents/ is gitignored by design - project agents are DERIVED from skillcentral by install.sh - so an agent following its Stage 9 instruction to update its persona edits a throwaway copy. RIGHTS-03 spotted this itself and tried to rescue its edit to the main checkout, which is also gitignored, so the rescue failed too. The CEO swept all 12 Sprint 05 worktrees: exactly one real loss, 30 lines of managing-editor lesson, recovered to the real source. One other file showed 340 changed lines and was PURE CRLF.
learnings.why: Sprint 04's retro celebrated 'the team updated its own documents, at scale' on the strength of six commits. Those were real because they were made in the buddy checkout. Any agent that edited its persona from inside a worktree in any earlier sprint lost the edit silently, and no check would have shown it.

learnings.finding: THE REVIEW GATE REVERSED A DONE ITEM AND THE REVERSAL WAS RIGHT. PLAT-18 reported done after merging three PRs. The CEO ran the actual defect against the live tracker rather than reading the report, and the colliding add was ACCEPTED - overwriting CONT-13 in place, the sprint's 12-point flagship, title replaced and 12pt to 1pt. All four evidence entries survived because PLAT-15's append-only guarantee held; the scoped fields were restored from sprint-05.json. The agent went back and shipped a fix that refuses in BOTH scopes, which the CEO then re-tested against a throwaway key first so a second failure could not damage the flagship again.
learnings.file_changed: buddy/CLAUDE.md gained a section on per-scope key uniqueness, written by the agent
learnings.why: The probe cost real damage and was still worth running. The alternative was a sprint that recorded a collision fix which did not fix collisions, and PLAT-16 was already lost to this defect in Sprint 04 with nothing saying so.

learnings.finding: AGENTS CORRECTED THE CEO ON MATTERS OF FACT REPEATEDLY, AND WERE RIGHT EVERY TIME. UI-18 disproved the premise the CEO wrote into its own brief - the contents list shipped on 63 of 86 articles, not 0 of 85 - and corrected it AT SOURCE in ceo-memory.md rather than only in its log. DES-18 disproved the CEO's stated premise for its gate: covers are 1600x1200 on 69 of 86, not 86 of 86. CONT-16 found that its own first extraction of a page was wrong in the FLATTERING direction and said so. RIGHTS-02's finding that four institutions are credited, not two, was confirmed by the CEO on live HTML after a first CEO check missed it entirely.
learnings.file_changed: docs/boardroom/ceo-memory.md, corrected at source by the agents rather than annotated
learnings.why: Sprint 02's retro recorded that corrections arrive INSIDE deliverables rather than as escalations, and that a skimmed report costs more than a slow one. This sprint that held: every one of these was in a work-done log or an evidence block, not in a message.

learnings.finding: GATES ALLOWED TO KILL AN ITEM FIRED TWICE AND BOTH REFUSALS WERE CORRECT. CONT-16 stopped with zero articles: both reserved families failed decision 170's 220/month floor AND were already owned by live pages, one of which nobody knew about and which already carried the exact artefact the brief asked for. It shipped scripts/seo/check-family-owned.py instead - cluster-method rule 4 as a runnable gate, which CONT-07 asked for on 28 Aug and never got. RIGHTS-03 stopped with the CDN clause open rather than claiming a takedown while six URLs still returned 200 HIT.
learnings.why: A parked item costs 5 points. A fabricated one costs the thing the product sells. Both agents were explicitly told a park with a clear reason was a good outcome, and both took it.

learnings.finding: git worktree remove IS NOT ATOMIC ON WINDOWS. It deregisters the worktree and then fails to delete the files, so `git worktree list` reads clean while the tree is still on disk. PLAT-19 found six such directories from earlier sprints holding 78,682 files, invisible to git, unnoticed for six sprints. The session swept 188,450 files across both workspaces after a two-signal check on every directory, losing zero registered worktrees.
learnings.file_changed: scripts/audit-worktree-shipped.sh --verify-gone (PLAT-19), plus scripts/measure/orphan-blob-check.py added this session
learnings.why: The right question for a deregistered directory is not 'does this differ from master' - stale checkouts always do - but 'was this content EVER committed'. Hashing each file and asking the object database answers it in one call and is the only signal that survives git no longer knowing the tree.

process_findings: THE PLANNING PASS MISSED A THIRD OF THE SPRINT AND THE OWNER APPROVED IT ANYWAY. The CEO built the Sprint 05 proposal from the sprint files, the Sprint 04 retro and ceo-memory.md, and NEVER RAN `sprint backlog`. Nine items totalling 27 points - all carried forward by Sprint 04's own retro, including a live production defect where a soft-failed pillar render caches forever - were never shown to the owner, who approved '81 points, full scope' believing that was everything. /startsprint's Step 0 caught it, hours later. This is the same shape as decision 167 and decision 94 before it: the backlog is a source the planning pass does not read, exactly as docs/plans/README.md's BLOCKED rows were until 30 Aug. THE SAME PASS ALSO CREATED SIX DUPLICATE ROWS by seeding the sprint with `sprint import`, which CREATES items, where `sprint plan <KEY> --sprint N` MOVES the existing one - and those duplicates then blocked four items from carrying forward cleanly at close, which PLAT-18's new refusal caught rather than silently overwriting. WHAT HELD: no item was marked done on an agent's report. All ten were verified by the CEO against live production or by running the item's own committed instrument, and the two that failed verification were reversed (PLAT-18) or held short (SEO-13, UI-17). The owner was never the critical path: the two owner-only items - closing PR #37 and the Cloudflare purge - were surfaced the moment they appeared, with the credential checked against the vault FIRST so the escalation carried a diagnosis rather than a question. WHAT DID NOT HOLD: wave 2 was never dispatched. Fourteen items, half the sprint, never left the backlog, and the sprint closes having attempted the half it dispatched.
shipped_check: EVERY COMPLETED ITEM IS VISIBLE TO THE OWNER, verified at close across three checkouts and every worktree: hellokahwin-site, hellokahwin (docs) and buddy all report 0 dirty and 0 unpushed. Live and checkable: six new articles taking the sitemap 103 -> 109 (CONT-13); the homepage passing its own H6 gate with 'VERDICT: H6 holds' where the same command exited 1 before the sprint (UI-13); a contents list on every article carrying two or more h2 with 900 anchors and 0 dangling (UI-18); FAQ coverage 47 -> 74+ present with 327 emitted questions (SEO-13); a 528x396 mid-size cover variant serving all twelve homepage thumbnails for a 375,060 byte SAVING above the fold (DES-18); the hantaran-kahwin seed re-angled onto definition and money (CONT-14); rule H6 written as an enforceable constraint with six fixtures (DES-17); the boundary guard installable from a fresh clone and refusing a cross-space checkout with exit 1 (RISK-10); a photographer-grouped rights census over 92 articles (RIGHTS-02); thirteen stale worktrees removed by two content signals with the one holding production undo records correctly kept (PLAT-19); and a tracker that refuses a colliding add in both scopes (PLAT-18). FIVE items had to be MERGED onto the docs line by the CEO before this was true.
